Issue:
Automation is generally seen as a sign of progress, but what is lost when we replace humans with machines?

Intelligent Machines
Many of the goods and services we depend on daily are now supplied by intelligent, automated machines rather than human beings. Robots build cars and other goods on assembly lines, where once there were human workers. Many of our phone conversations are now conducted not with people but with sophisticated technologies. We can now buy goods at a variety of stores without the help of a human cashier. Automation is generally seen as a sign of progress, but what is lost when we replace humans with machines? Given the accelerating variety and prevalence of intelligent machines, it is worth examining the implications and meaning of their presence in our lives.
Perspective One (Dystopian view)
What we lose with the replacement of people by machines is some part of our own humanity. Even our mundane daily encounters no longer require from us basic courtesy, respect, and tolerance for other people.
Perspective Two (Utilitarian view)
Machines are good at low-skill, repetitive jobs, and at high-speed, extremely precise jobs. In both cases they work better than humans. This efficiency leads to a more prosperous and progressive world for everyone.
Perspective Three (Progressive view)
Intelligent machines challenge our long-standing ideas about what humans are or can be. This is good because it pushes both humans and machines toward new, unimagined possibilities.

state your own perspective on the issue, and analyze the relationship between your perspective and at least one other perspective on the issue.

With the advent of AC/DC electricity, satirists claimed it was dangerous. With cellphones, some writers speculated they would cause cancer. Today, the speculations and fears continue to circulate as new technologies emerge.

With change, inevitably, comes loss and the unknown. The status quo, is lost when a technology changes the way society does something. For instance the status quo had been walking or taking horse back or horse-powered vehichles. That changed when cars began to impact the way people moved. With cars, we lost the status quo and we lost an entire industry of commonplace horse ownership. When the car is first introduced, people sense the unknown depths of potential change. The possibility of change, the potential for loss, and the unknown extent to which these might occur make dissurptive technologies appear as a threat to those who are change adverse and sensitive to a fear of the unknown. 

To those who are less change adverse and to those who are less sensitive to a few of the unknown, technologies can perceived through a lens of potential. Most technologies are developed with the intent to do a good and helpful task.  For those who are unafraid, the promosing potential outweighs the potential for loss. 

With the advent of each new technology these potentials must be considered through a lens of logic rather than fear or hope. In fear, some have responded to the use of AI with a belief that artificial intellegence will cause humans to have fewer human-to-human interactions and, as such, the communications skills required for such interactions will diminish. Setting fear aside and reviewing this arguement logically, we can see the examples of ways that other technologies have already had a similar impact on a large portion of our population. For instance, social media and personal cellphones have diminished the upcoming generations interpersonal communication skills. 

However, to determine whether or not we can expect this outcome from AI and whether we can anticipate this outcome doing signficant harm to our society would require further research. Recognizing that potential exists is wise while proceeding with AI design.

I would leap unknowningly into the future of machine learning and artificial intellegence unconcerned for the jobs that may be lost, the changes it may make on our society, or any unpredictable impact it may have.
